title: Was the croissant born to celebrate an Ottoman defeat?
titulo: Was the croissant born to celebrate an Ottoman defeat?

sources.cita_corta: Europeana, The History of the Croissant

scenes.narration: A widely repeated story claims the croissant was invented to celebrate the Ottoman defeat during the siege of Vienna in 1683.
scenes.image_credit: Croissants au beurre (18953292873). Herry Wibisono (herryway), CC0. Wikimedia Commons. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Croissants_au_beurre_(18953292873).jpg

scenes.narration: The legend says Viennese bakers, working before dawn, discovered an attack and raised the alarm. To celebrate, they created a bread shaped like a crescent moon, an Ottoman symbol.
scenes.image_credit: Martin Battle of Vienna. Pierre-Denis Martin, Public domain. Wikimedia Commons. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Martin_Battle_of_Vienna.jpg

scenes.narration: The problem is that there are no reliable documents confirming that story. It is an appealing tale, but not documented history.
scenes.image_credit: Vienna assediata dalle Armi Ottomane gli 12 Lugliio 1683. Giovanni Giacomo de Rossi, Public domain. Wikimedia Commons. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Vienna_assediata_dalle_Armi_Ottomane_gli_12_Lugliio_1683.jpg
scenes.visual_description: File:Vienna assediata dalle Armi Ottomane gli 12 Lugliio 1683.jpg

scenes.narration: What we do know is that Austria had breads called kipferl, shaped like a crescent, long before the modern croissant became popular in France.
scenes.image_credit: Topfenkolatsche und Wiener Kipferl IMG 7585. Politikaner, CC BY-SA 3.0. Wikimedia Commons. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Topfenkolatsche_und_Wiener_Kipferl_IMG_7585.JPG

scenes.narration: In the 19th century, the Austrian businessman August Zang opened a Viennese bakery in Paris. His products helped spread the crescent-shaped bread.
scenes.image_credit: Boulangerie de Paris, XIXe siècle, NJ9828(3). Unknown authorUnknown author, CC0. Wikimedia Commons · original: Paris Musées. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Boulangerie_de_Paris,_XIXe_si%C3%A8cle,_NJ9828(3).jpg
scenes.visual_description: File:Boulangerie de Paris, XIXe siècle, NJ9828(3).jpg

scenes.narration: The modern croissant developed in France from Central European traditions. The story of the siege of Vienna is a legend without solid evidence.
scenes.image_credit: Croissant 3. Maffeth.opiana, CC BY-SA 4.0. Wikimedia Commons. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Croissant_3.jpg
